title: What if Earth had rings like Saturn?
premise: Earth suddenly has a wide, bright ring system made of ice and rock, like Saturn's.

intro.title: What if Earth had *rings* like Saturn?
intro.subtitle: A HYPOTHETICAL SCENARIO

tooltip.label: FACT
tooltip.text: Saturn's main rings are mostly water ice, and in places only about 10 meters thick.

beats.caption: Saturn's rings are huge, but incredibly thin.
Now give Earth a ring just like it, circling above the equator.
Standing right on the equator, you'd see the ring edge-on: a thin line straight overhead.
Farther north or south, it becomes a giant glowing arch across the sky.
Lit by the Sun, the ring would make nights far brighter than they are today.
In winter, the ring could cast its shadow over half a hemisphere, making winters colder.
Satellites would have to avoid the ring, or get shredded crossing it.

tooltip.label: REAL SCIENCE
tooltip.text: Some scientists think Earth may have had a ring of its own about 466 million years ago.

beats.caption: And it may have happened before.
